10.	The Dutch are famous for being tall, but their country is famously short on elevation. The nation barely rises above sea level — a third of it actually lies below sea level. And yet the Dutch celebrate their "highest peak" Vaalserberg with two observation towers, a labyrinth, souvenir shops, and a café that cheekily calls itself "the only mountain hut in the Netherlands." This "peak" stands at a grand 322 meters — shorter than most communications towers. Vaalserberg is located in the province of Limburg, at the extreme southeastern tip of the country, far from the flat polders and windmills that define the Dutch image. Between 1830 and 1919, a curious fourth territory called Neutral Moresnet — a tiny condominium created because Prussia and the Netherlands couldn't agree on who owned a zinc mine — made this summit even more unusual. Today the road on the Dutch side is still called the Viergrenzenweg, a vestige of that forgotten micro-state.
